To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rats which preferred alcohol had decreased insulin levels and lower glucokinase activity, which was accompanied by increased glucose phosphorylation via hexokinas and lower insulin sensitivity to glucose, as well as higher resistance to starvation.
the ethanol-consuming rats were more sensitive to the effects of starvation and had a higher rate of glucose phosphorylation by hexokinase, and lower rate of glucose phosphorylating by glucokinase.

the rats with different preferences of ethanol consumption are characterized by the distinct features of their carbohydrate metabolism, including the decreased level of immunorreactive insulin in the blood serum as well the decreased glucokinase activity in the liver tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms underlying the development of ethanol preference.
the study of the relationship between the metabolism of alcohol and the metabolism of glucose.
the search of the biochemical mechanisms of ethanol consumption.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the differences in glucose metabolism are responsible for the differences in alcohol consumption in rats.

the increased ethanol intake by rats is a result of the specific properties of the glucose metabolism, which in turn is responsible for a decreased sensitivity to the effects of glucose on insulin release.

the increased alcohol consumption in ethanol-consuming rats may be explained by a combination of the following factors: a) the reduced sensitivity of the insulin-dependent glucose metabolism, b) the increased resistance of the insulin-dependent metabolism to fasting, c) the increased activity of the non-insulin-dependent glucose metabolism, and d) the increased activity and sensitivity of the alcohol metabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ethanol-consuming rats are more efficient in the utilization of ethanol than in the use of glucose.

the increased ethanol consumption is due to the increased activity of alcohol dehydrogenase and decreased activity of the insulin system, as well as the decreased activity of glucokinase in the ethanol-consuming animals.
the increased consumption of ethanol is a consequence of the specific properties of glucose metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consumption of alcohol can be associated with the metabolic disorders of glucose and insulin, which may be the reason of the increased risk of diabetes in alcoholics.

the characteristic properties in glucose metabolism in ethanol-preferring rats appear to be the result of a selection for increased alcohol consumption, which is metabolized in pathways that do not involve the glyco- lytic pathway.
the characteristics of glucose metabolism in animals with a high preference for ethanol consumption are different from those in animals with a low preference for ethanol consumption.
